presentingComplaint: New fever, purulent tracheal secretions and worsening oxygenation on day 6 of mechanical ventilation
history: Admitted 6 days ago to the medical ICU with acute-on-chronic respiratory failure and intubated for airway protection following a large territory ischaemic stroke. Sedated and mechanically ventilated since. Over the last 24 hours the bedside team notes new-onset fever, an increase in the volume and purulence of tracheal aspirate, and a rising FiO2 and PEEP requirement to maintain saturations. Received a course of piperacillin-tazobactam for a urinary source earlier in the admission. PMH: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, ex-smoker. No known drug allergies.
examination: Sedated, intubated, RASS -3. New coarse crepitations and bronchial breathing at the right base. Copious thick yellow-green secretions on suctioning. No calf swelling; no rash. Pertinent negatives: no new murmur, no abdominal tenderness, catheter site clean, no peripheral stigmata of endocarditis.
imaging: Portable CXR: new right lower and middle lobe air-space opacification with air bronchograms, not present on admission film; no large effusion or pneumothorax
microbiology: Endotracheal aspirate Gram stain: numerous polymorphs with Gram-negative bacilli; semi-quantitative culture and sensitivities pending. Two sets of blood cultures sent. Urinary Legionella/pneumococcal antigen negative.
finalDiagnosis: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (late-onset, MDR risk factors present)
citations: IDSA/ATS Management of Adults with Hospital-Acquired and Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia 2016
stewardship: Empiric broad-spectrum cover for late-onset VAP (>5 days ventilation) with MDR risk (prior IV antibiotics within 90 days): antipseudomonal beta-lactam such as piperacillin-tazobactam or cefepime/meropenem PLUS an antipseudomonal second agent, and add anti-MRSA cover (vancomycin or linezolid) given prior antibiotic exposure and severity. De-escalate on endotracheal aspirate culture/sensitivity and stop at 7 days if responding.
contraindications: Beta-lactam anaphylaxis would preclude piperacillin-tazobactam/cefepime - use aztreonam-based regimen
Vancomycin requires renal-adjusted dosing and level monitoring; linezolid preferred if AKI or concurrent nephrotoxins
Avoid empiric aminoglycoside monotherapy for pneumonia
edgeCases: Ventilator-associated tracheobronchitis presents identically but without new radiographic infiltrate
Low-burden semi-quantitative culture may reflect colonisation rather than true VAP - correlate clinically
Non-infective ventilator-associated events (ARDS, fluid overload, atelectasis) can mimic VAP and inflate antibiotic use
expectedMaiK: Late-onset VAP (day 6 of ventilation) with prior antibiotic exposure carries MDR risk, so IDSA/ATS 2016 favours empiric antipseudomonal plus anti-MRSA cover guided by the unit antibiogram, followed by de-escalation on culture and a 7-day course if the patient improves.
expectedNextQuestions: When was mechanical ventilation started relative to symptom onset (>48h and >5 days)?
What antibiotics has the patient received in the last 90 days and any prior resistant isolates?
What is the local ICU antibiogram / MDR prevalence?
expectedInvestigations: Endotracheal aspirate or BAL for semi-quantitative culture and sensitivities
Serial CXR and PaO2:FiO2, WBC, procalcitonin trend

investigations: Endotracheal aspirate / BAL culture and sensitivity

regressionAssertions: stewardship tier must be broad with antipseudomonal + anti-MRSA empiric cover
differential must not collapse to CAP as primary given >48h ventilation
